Description.Summary: Glean Agents is an enterprise AI agent platform that automates workplace tasks by building, deploying, orchestrating, and governing AI agents across workflows. It functions as a horizontal environment for creating autonomous agents that handle multi-step workflows using natural language, enterprise context, and a library of actions. The platform is deployed as an enterprise SaaS product integrated into web applications, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and developer tools, supporting agents for engineering, sales, HR, and other business functions.

evidence.quote: Glean Agents automate your work simply using natural language.
Glean Agents are AI-powered tools that automate tasks from simple to complex workflows, by handling actions like gathering information, summarizing data, and making decisions based on previous steps.
Glean is the Work AI platform connected to your enterprise's data, providing capabilities for search, assistants, and AI agents.
Glean Agents is the horizontal environment for building, deploying, orchestrating, and governing AI agents in the enterprise.

Practices.Summary: Glean heavily tests all layers of their search stack with each release qualification going through a battery of end-to-end search tests on fully loaded deployments. They have invested in quickly bootstrapping an in-memory multi-node search engine within unit tests to verify changes rapidly. The team runs test queries on any new search engine before proceeding with switchover and runs the same verification procedure on the active search engine before deleting the old one for rollback safety. The most impactful improvements to AI agents come from a structured feedback loop: refining instructions, structuring context, tuning model parameters, and selecting the right language models.

Practices.Summary: Glean implemented dynamic code loading with version tags to avoid server restarts during ranking code updates. They remap build artifacts with release tags and upload to the cloud in seconds, enabling nightly internal deployments and weekly customer rollouts. Practices.Summary: Glean introduced a structured Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC) mirroring software engineering standards with seven distinct stages—Opportunity, Design, Performance, Context, Develop, Launch, and Monitor & Improve. Agents should be well-designed, tested, rolled out carefully, monitored in production, and improved over time in the same way that engineering teams deliver other types of enterprise-grade software. As the startup grew, they introduced more processes to execute engineering with stability after acquiring paying customers, and the engineering team naturally split from one unified team into specialized teams.

Practices.Summary: Glean tracks documentation freshness with metadata update practices. Content typically appears in search within a few minutes of indexing. Crawl Rate and Change Rate metrics update approximately every 5–10 minutes, with Change Rate indicating ongoing freshness based on user-driven changes synced in the past 24 hours. The platform allows attaching structured metadata to documents from any datasource and offers a Custom Metadata API for tagging and classifying documents without re-indexing.
